knowledge:
- key_parameters: baseDir=Path to the directory containing the output files from an alevin run. Must retain the original directory structure ;; sampleId=Character string specifying the sample identifier used in the report ;; outputFile=Character string specifying the name of the output report file (e.g., "alevinReport.html") ;; outputFormat=Format of the output report, such as "html_document" or "pdf_document" ;; outputDir=Directory where the generated report should be saved ;; forceOverwrite=Logical indicating whether to overwrite an existing report file with the same name
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package after running Salmon-Alevin on single-cell RNA-seq data to perform quality control checks, visualize cell barcode collapse, assess mapping/deduplication rates, and inspect knee plots of UMI counts and gene counts.
- pitfalls: Moving or renaming the output files from alevin will cause errors, as alevinQC assumes a strict directory structure ;; To generate the full set of files required for alevinQC, alevin must be run with the --dumpFeatures flag ;; Processing output from Salmon v0.14 or later requires Alevin v1.1 or later ;; To export data from the Shiny app, users must click the 'Close app' button in the top right corner rather than just closing the window.

workflows.name: static_qc_report
workflows.intent: Validate alevin output files and generate a static HTML or PDF quality control report.
input: baseDir (Alevin output directory containing alevin/ and aux_info/ subdirectories and cmd_info.json)
workflows.stages: 1. Check that all required alevin files are available using checkAlevinInputFiles() ;; 2. Generate the QC report using alevinQCReport()
workflows.code:
baseDir <- system.file("extdata/alevin_example_v0.14", package = "alevinQC")
checkAlevinInputFiles(baseDir = baseDir)
outputDir <- tempdir()
alevinQCReport(baseDir = baseDir, sampleId = "testSample", 
               outputFile = "alevinReport.html", 
               outputFormat = "html_document",
               outputDir = outputDir, forceOverwrite = TRUE)

workflows.name: interactive_shiny_app
workflows.intent: Launch an interactive Shiny application for visual quality control and optionally export the underlying data.
input: baseDir (Alevin output directory containing alevin/ and aux_info/ subdirectories and cmd_info.json)
workflows.stages: 1. Create the Shiny app object using alevinQCShiny() ;; 2. Run the app using shiny::runApp() and capture the output

workflows.name: custom_plotting_and_data_extraction
workflows.intent: Read alevin QC data into R to inspect summary tables and generate individual diagnostic plots.
input: baseDir (Alevin output directory containing alevin/ and aux_info/ subdirectories and cmd_info.json)
workflows.stages: 1. Read the alevin output into an R object using readAlevinQC() ;; 2. Inspect cell barcode tables and summary tables ;; 3. Generate individual plots using plotAlevinKneeRaw(), plotAlevinBarcodeCollapse(), plotAlevinQuant(), and plotAlevinKneeNbrGenes()
workflows.code:
alevin <- readAlevinQC(baseDir = baseDir)
head(alevin$cbTable)
knitr::kable(alevin$summaryTables$fullDataset)
knitr::kable(alevin$summaryTables$initialWhitelist)
knitr::kable(alevin$summaryTables$finalWhitelist)
knitr::kable(alevin$versionTable)
plotAlevinKneeRaw(alevin$cbTable)
plotAlevinBarcodeCollapse(alevin$cbTable)
plotAlevinQuant(alevin$cbTable)
plotAlevinKneeNbrGenes(alevin$cbTable)
